Landed. Deployed **v0.4.170**, live daemon up on it (pid 1364199), 45/45 checks green — including a run against the bytes the daemon is actually serving (fetched from :8795, not the checkout).

WHAT SHIPPED
Cards: radius --r-md(12) -> --r-2xl(20), padding --sp-4 all round, --sec fill and the 10px gap unchanged; a 36px --r-md tile leads the row, recessed to --bg (the treatment the chips inside the same card already use) and carrying the existing status dot at 12px. Name 16 -> 14 (--t-sub, semibold kept); task and foot untouched. Card contents byte-identical to HEAD, measured.
Pill: static markup, sibling of the tab, showTab toggles it. Fixed bottom-right at --sp-4 + safe-area, 40px, stadium radius, --btn/--btn-text, z-index 3, no shadow, no entrance motion. Old dashed row and its rule deleted; the list now starts at the panel's own 12px under the tab bar.
Relief: the tab reserves --fab-h + two gutters, so at full scroll the last card clears the pill by 26px (16 reserved + the card's own margin).

PROOF — scripts/webapp-measure/sessions.mjs
On a pre-change page 36 checks FAIL and it still runs to completion (every pill read is null-safe, so a control run prints a readable column instead of dying on the first). The layering half could not be proven that way — the old page has no pill, so "it paints above the list" would pass vacuously — so it carries its own falsifiers: the elementFromPoint probe re-run with the pill at z-index -1 (must report the list on top), and the relief re-measured with the reserved padding stripped (the last card must then be caught under it). Plus the one the design turns on: the pill's node identity held across a full 4s poll cycle — same element after the list is wiped and rebuilt.
Contents guard: the same fixture through both pages, every card's text compared to HEAD's. Passes on both, by design — that is what says the change is shape only.

SHOTS -> /home/ubuntu/.claude/channels/telegram/agent-bus/dm/shared/sessions-restyle/
sessions-{before,after}-{dark,light}.png plus after-{dark,light}-bottom.png (the end of the list, where the relief is the whole claim). Light theme included because the app themes off Telegram's injected vars, not prefers-color-scheme — the recessed tile inverts to white-on-grey there and reads fine.

ALSO
CLAUDE.md gained the invariant paragraph (why the pill is outside the list, why the reserved padding is its licence to float, the z-index ladder, no-shadow/no-motion) and the measure README the script's entry.

NOT DONE, deliberately: no commit. Deployed-but-uncommitted is the owner's staging area. When he approves: webapp/index.html, CLAUDE.md, scripts/webapp-measure/README.md, .claude-plugin/{plugin,marketplace}.json and a `git add` of the new scripts/webapp-measure/sessions.mjs (untracked, so it did not ship in the deploy — scripts do not need to).
Real-device observation is his — I can render and hit-test the served page, I cannot open Telegram. If he wants the </> glyph instead of the dot in the tile it is two lines and a re-run.

items.text:
The restyle is live — v0.4.170, screenshots above. All 45 checks pass, including runs against the bytes the daemon is actually serving, and the proof went beyond the usual: the "pill floats above the list" claim was falsified both ways (dropping the pill's z-index makes the check fail, stripping the scroll relief makes the last card get caught under it), and the contents guard confirms every card's text is byte-identical to before — the change is genuinely shape-only. The status dot now lives in each card's icon tile; if you'd rather have the `</>` glyph like your reference, it's a two-line swap.

Three things sit with you: a look on your actual device (the session can render and hit-test the served page but can't open Telegram itself), the commit — deployed-but-uncommitted is staged for your approval as usual — and that glyph veto if you want it.

Meanwhile I've dispatched the queued thoughts task: restore a distinct visual treatment for narration in the mini-app chat, starting with a live check of how it presents today, then a design note before any build.
